l: house of Israel, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The house of Israel will suffer calamity and destruction, but the Lord will remember his covenant with it after it has been driven and scattered. The Gentiles are described as having care for the house of Israel.

l: seed of Jacob, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The seed of Jacob will be scattered and become a dark, filthy, and loathsome people because of unbelief and idolatry. A remnant of the seed of Jacob may later go among the Gentiles as a lion if they do not repent.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: Jesus is described as the Christ and the Son of the living God. The Nephites might have been clasped in his arms, and the Jews are to be persuaded to believe in him.

l: God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: God created the Nephites, leads his people, and has power to roll the earth together as a scroll. He will remember his covenants and the prayers of the righteous, and will act in justice against the unrepentant.

l: Satan, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: Satan leads the people who were once a delightsome people and had Christ for their shepherd. They are driven about by Satan as chaff before the wind or a vessel without sail, anchor, or steering.

l: land of their inheritance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The Lord gave the land of their inheritance to the Jews, or all the house of Israel. The Father will restore them to that land through Jesus in fulfillment of the covenant.

l: gospel of Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The gospel will go forth from the Gentiles to the seed of the people. It is intended to help that seed more fully believe.

l: covenant of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The Lord will remember the covenant he made with Abraham and all the house of Israel after the people have been driven and scattered by the Gentiles.

l: destruction of the Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The destruction of the Nephites occurs after the Lamanites overcome them in battle. Mormon writes about the bloodshed and carnage in an abridged form because of the commandment he received and to limit sorrow over the people's wickedness.

l: scattering of the Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The Nephites are scattered by the Gentiles, and the Gentiles are said to scatter this people. Their scattering precedes the Lord's remembrance of his covenant with Abraham and all the house of Israel.

l: Lamanite invasions, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The Lamanites come against the Nephites repeatedly, including attacks on the city of Jordan and other cities. Their invasions destroy lands and inhabitants that were not gathered in and eventually overwhelm the Nephite armies.

l: repentance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The Nephites do not repent of their iniquities, and Mormon knows the judgments that will come upon them. The Gentiles are commanded to repent, turn from their evil ways, and humble themselves before God.

l: unbelief and idolatry, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The seed of the people becomes dark, filthy, and loathsome because of unbelief and idolatry. The Spirit of the Lord has ceased to strive with their fathers, who are without Christ and God in the world.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: Mormon finishes his record concerning the destruction of the Nephites and leads the remaining people to the land of Cumorah for a final battle against the Lamanites. The Lamanites destroy nearly all the Nephites, leaving Mormon, Moroni, twenty and four survivors, and a few others who escaped or deserted. Mormon hides the sacred records in the hill Cumorah, gives a few plates to Moroni, and mourns the fallen people. He teaches that the dead will become immortal and stand before the judgment-seat of Christ, and that repentance before the destruction could have prevented their fall.

l: Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: Mormon finishes his record concerning the destruction of the Nephites, leads his people to the land of Cumorah, and writes to the king of the Lamanites to request a gathering there. He hides the entrusted records in the hill Cumorah, keeps a few plates for Moroni, survives the battle wounded, and mourns the slain.

l: Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The Nephites gather with their wives and children in the land of Cumorah for their last struggle against the Lamanites. Nearly all are slain, while twenty and four survive with Mormon and a few others escape or desert.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The Lamanites grant Mormon's request to gather at Cumorah and then march against the Nephites. Their armies kill nearly all of Mormon's people.

l: land of Cumorah, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The land of Cumorah is where the Nephites gather for their final battle. It is described as a land of many waters, rivers, and fountains.

l: hill Cumorah, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The hill Cumorah is the location around which the Nephites pitch their tents and from which the survivors view the slain. Mormon hides the records entrusted to him in the hill Cumorah.

l: battle, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The final battle at Cumorah is fought with swords, bows, arrows, axes, and other weapons of war. The Lamanites overwhelm the Nephites, killing nearly all of them.

l: records, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: Mormon is commanded not to let the sacred records fall into the hands of the Lamanites because they would destroy them. He hides the records in the hill Cumorah and gives a few plates to Moroni.

l: Moroni, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: Moroni is Mormon's son and is among the twenty and four survivors of the battle. Mormon gives him a few plates, and ten thousand of Moroni's people are also described as having been led by him.

l: armies of the Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The armies of the Lamanites march toward the Nephites and attack them with great numbers and many weapons. They leave nearly all the Nephites dead after the battle.

l: twenty and four survivors, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The twenty and four survivors are the remaining group with Mormon after the Lamanites have slain the Nephites. Among them is Mormon's son Moroni.

l: destruction of the Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The destruction of the Nephites occurs in the final battle at Cumorah. Nearly all the people are killed, and their flesh, bones, and blood are left upon the earth to molder and return to their mother earth.

l: anguish and mourning, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: Mormon's soul is rent with anguish because of the slain Nephites. He cries out in mourning over their rejection of Jesus and laments that his sorrows cannot bring them back.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: Jesus is described as having stood with open arms to receive the fallen Nephites. Mormon says they would not have fallen if they had not rejected him.

l: repentance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: Mormon wishes that the Nephites had repented before the great destruction came upon them. He teaches that repentance could have prevented their fall.

l: judgment, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The dead will become incorruptible and stand before the judgment-seat of Christ. They will be judged according to their works, and the righteous will be blessed with their fathers.

l: Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The Lord commands Mormon not to allow the sacred records entrusted to him to fall into the hands of the Lamanites. Mormon says the Nephites departed from the ways of the Lord.

l: Eternal Father of heaven, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 6
s: The Eternal Father of heaven knows the state of the fallen Nephites. He does with them according to his justice and mercy.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The speaker addresses the remnant of this people, identified as a remnant of the house of Israel and the seed of Jacob. They are told to repent, lay down their weapons of war, learn of their fathers, believe in Jesus Christ, and be baptized. Jesus Christ is described as the Son of God who was slain, rose again, overcame the grave, and brings about the resurrection of the dead and the redemption of the world. Those who believe in Christ and are baptized with water, fire, and the Holy Ghost will fare well in the day of judgment.

l: God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: God may give the speaker words for the remnant of this people. God may command them to take up their weapons of war again.

l: remnant of this people, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The remnant of this people is addressed so that they may know of the things of their fathers. It is told to repent, lay down its weapons of war, believe in Jesus Christ, and be baptized.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The remnant of this people is told that it is of the house of Israel.

l: repentance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The people must come unto repentance or they cannot be saved. They must repent of all their sins and iniquities.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: Jesus Christ is the Son of God who was slain by the Jews and rose again by the power of the Father. He gained the victory over the grave, swallowed up the sting of death, brings to pass the resurrection of the dead, and brought to pass the redemption of the world.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The resurrection of the dead is brought to pass by Jesus Christ. Through it, man must be raised to stand before the judgment-seat.

l: judgment, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: At the judgment day, the person found guiltless before Jesus Christ is given to dwell in the presence of God in his kingdom.

l: redemption of the world, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: Jesus Christ has brought to pass the redemption of the world. It allows the guiltless to dwell in the presence of God in his kingdom and sing ceaseless praises.

l: Eternal Father of heaven, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The Father is one with the Son and the Holy Ghost as one God. Jesus Christ was raised again by the power of the Father.

l: Son, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The Son is one with the Father and the Holy Ghost as one God. The guiltless sing ceaseless praises unto the Son.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The Holy Ghost is one with the Father and the Son as one God. Believers are to be baptized with the Holy Ghost after being baptized with water.

l: gospel of Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The people are told to lay hold upon the gospel of Christ. It is set before them in this record and in the record that will come unto the Gentiles from the Jews and from the Gentiles unto them.

l: record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The record contains the gospel of Christ and is written so that people may believe in it and know concerning their fathers and the marvelous works wrought by the power of God among them.

l: Gentiles, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: A record will come unto the Gentiles from the Jews, and that record will come from the Gentiles unto the remnant of this people.

l: seed of Jacob, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The people are told that they are a remnant of the seed of Jacob. Therefore, they are numbered among the people of the first covenant.

l: baptism, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The people are told to be baptized in the name of Jesus. Baptism is to be first with water and then with fire and with the Holy Ghost, following the example and commandment of the Savior.

l: death, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: In Jesus Christ, the sting of death is swallowed up. Jesus Christ has gained the victory over the grave.

l: salvation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 7
s: The people cannot be saved unless they come unto repentance. Belief in Christ and baptism are presented as part of what will make it well with them in the day of judgment.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Moroni finishes the record of Mormon after the Nephites are destroyed and hides the records in the earth. He describes the Lamanites, the land’s continual war, murder, and bloodshed, and the disappearance of the disciples of Jesus. Moroni prophesies that the record will come forth by the power of God amid widespread unbelief, wickedness, pride, pollution, and churches built for gain. He warns that the Lord will remember his covenant, fulfill his promises, and bring vengeance upon those who oppress the saints and the needy.

l: Moroni, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Moroni finishes the record of Mormon, remains alone after the destruction of his people, and writes and hides the records in the earth. He warns future people about pride, wickedness, polluted churches, and oppression of the poor and needy.

l: Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Mormon made the record and commanded Moroni to finish it. He was killed in battle along with Moroni’s kinsfolk.

l: Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The Nephites who escaped the battle at Cumorah were hunted by the Lamanites until they were destroyed. Moroni describes their fall and destruction as great and marvelous.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The Lamanites hunted the Nephites from city to city until they were no more. They were also at war one with another.

l: battle at Cumorah, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: After the great and tremendous battle at Cumorah, the surviving Nephites were hunted and destroyed.

l: Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The Lord commands Moroni, remembers covenants, brings records out of darkness, and fulfills eternal purposes and promises. He judges, repays, and brings vengeance upon the wicked.

l: God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: God is the true God, knows all things, and gives power for the record to come forth. God’s word and power enable faithful people to perform mighty works.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Jesus Christ showed Moroni the people of a future day and revealed their actions to him.

l: disciples of Jesus, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The disciples of Jesus were the only people known to remain who knew the true God. They ministered to Mormon and Moroni before the Lord would not suffer them to remain with the people.

l: the Book of Mormon record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The record was made by Mormon, finished by Moroni, and hidden in the earth. It is of great worth and will come to light by the power of God, bringing greater knowledge to those who receive it without condemning its imperfections.

l: land, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The land became a place of continual murder and bloodshed, with only Lamanites and robbers remaining upon it.

l: war, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: War continued among the Lamanites, and no one knew when it would end.

l: murder and bloodshed, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The whole face of the land was characterized by continual murder and bloodshed.

l: covenant people of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The covenant people of the Lord are the house of Israel. Those who oppose the Lord’s work and seek to destroy them are in danger of being hewn down and cast into the fire.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The house of Israel is the covenant people of the Lord, and the Lord will remember the covenant made with them.

l: saints, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Saints who previously possessed the land will cry from the dust, and their prayers for their brethren and for the coming forth of the record are known to the Lord.

l: miracles, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The record will come forth in a day when people say miracles are done away. The text also describes faithful people removing mountains, shaking the earth, causing prisons to tumble, and being protected from fire, beasts, and serpents.

l: secret combinations, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Secret combinations and the works of darkness will cause the blood of saints to cry unto the Lord.

l: works of darkness, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The works of darkness, together with secret combinations, will bring about the cries of the blood of saints.

l: power of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The record will come forth by the power of God. This power also enabled faithful people to perform mighty acts and withstand dangers.

l: churches, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Churches become polluted through pride, love of money, fine apparel, and iniquity. Leaders and teachers rise in pride, and some churches are built to obtain gain.

l: holy church of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The holy church of God is polluted by teachers who sell themselves for that which will canker and are ashamed to take upon themselves the name of Christ.

l: holy word of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: People transfigure and pollute the holy word of God to bring damnation upon their souls.

l: word of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The word of God brings power, and the revelations of God will be fulfilled despite the wickedness of the people.

l: eternal purposes of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The eternal purposes of the Lord will roll on until all his promises are fulfilled.

l: promises of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The Lord’s promises will all be fulfilled, and no one can prevent them.

l: covenant of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The Lord will remember the covenant made with the ancient and long-dispersed covenant people.

l: blood of saints, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The blood of saints will cry unto the Lord because of secret combinations and works of darkness.

l: pollutions, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Pollutions will cover the earth, including murders, robbing, lying, deceiving, whoredoms, and other abominations.

l: abominations, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Abominations are built up to obtain gain, and people excuse wickedness by claiming that the Lord will uphold it at the last day.

l: churches built for gain, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Churches built for gain will say that people can come to them and be forgiven of their sins for money.

l: money, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: People love money and substance more than they love the poor, needy, sick, and afflicted. Money is also used by churches built for gain.

l: pride, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Pride causes churches, leaders, teachers, and people to become polluted and to engage in envy, strife, malice, persecution, and other iniquities.

l: fine apparel, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: People love and wear fine apparel and use it in adorning themselves and their churches while neglecting those in need.

l: poor, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The poor are loved less than money, substance, fine apparel, and church adornment, and are allowed to pass by without notice.

l: needy, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The needy are neglected while people pursue money, fine apparel, and the adornment of churches.

l: sick, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The sick are allowed to pass by unnoticed while people focus on worldly possessions and appearances.

l: afflicted, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The afflicted are neglected by people who value worldly praise and possessions over their welfare.

l: sword of vengeance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: The sword of vengeance hangs over the wicked, and the time soon comes when the Lord will avenge the blood of the saints.

l: Nephite vengeance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 8
s: Vengeance belongs to the Lord, who will repay and avenge the blood of the saints upon those responsible.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: This unit concerns unbelievers, those who deny revelations, and all people who will stand before Jesus Christ for judgment. It teaches that God is unchanging and remains a God of miracles, while miracles cease among people because of unbelief and departure from the right way. Jesus Christ’s disciples are commanded to preach the gospel, and believers are promised signs, salvation, and confirmation of Christ’s words. The record also explains its language, imperfections, purpose, and prayers for the restoration of the brethren and the fulfillment of God’s covenant with the house of Israel.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ is the Son of God and is also called the Father and the Son. His death brings the resurrection and redemption of man, and belief in his name is connected with answered prayer, salvation, and spiritual signs.

l: God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, without variableness or changing. He created the heavens, the earth, Adam, and all things in them, and he remains a God of miracles.

l: Eternal Father of heaven, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The Father is addressed in prayer in the name of Jesus Christ. He is asked to cleanse unbelievers, grant requested things, and remember the covenant made with the house of Israel.

l: Son, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The Son is identified as Jesus Christ, through whom came the redemption of man. Jesus Christ commands his disciples to preach the gospel and promises signs to those who believe.

l: the Lamb of God (Jesus Christ), The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The Lamb of God is the one before whom people will stand and whose holiness and glory will be revealed. His blood cleanses those who turn to the Lord and cry to the Father in the name of Jesus.

l: unbelievers, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Unbelievers are warned that they will face their guilt before God and the Lamb of God. They are urged to turn to the Lord, cry to the Father, and be cleansed by the blood of the Lamb.

l: revelations of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Revelations of God are not done away, contrary to what some people claim. Denying revelations, prophecies, gifts, healing, speaking with tongues, and their interpretation is described as ignorance of the gospel of Christ.

l: miracles, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Miracles were wrought by God, Jesus Christ, and the apostles. God has not ceased to be a God of miracles, but miracles cease among people when they dwindle in unbelief and depart from the right way.

l: gospel of Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The gospel of Christ is not understood by those who deny revelations and spiritual gifts. It is to be preached to every creature, and those who believe and are baptized shall be saved.

l: the scriptures, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The scriptures teach that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever. Those who deny revelations are said either not to have read the scriptures or not to understand them.

l: Adam, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Adam was created by God, and by Adam came the fall of man.

l: the apostles, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The apostles wrought many mighty miracles.

l: Jesus Christ's disciples, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ’s disciples are commanded to go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature. The command is given to disciples who should tarry and to all his disciples.

l: the children of men, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Miracles cease among the children of men because they dwindle in unbelief, depart from the right way, and do not know the God in whom they should trust.

l: all men, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: All men are redeemed from the endless sleep of temporal death through the resurrection. They will be awakened by the power of God and stand before his bar for judgment.

l: the children of Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The children of Christ are mentioned as people whom the despisers of the works of the Lord will despise. Such despisers are warned that they shall wonder and perish.

l: the saints, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The prayers of all the saints who have dwelt in the land concern the restoration of the brethren to the knowledge of Christ.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: God the Father is asked to remember the covenant he made with the house of Israel and to bless them forever through faith on the name of Jesus Christ.

l: the brethren, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The record is written partly concerning the restoration of the brethren to the knowledge of Christ. The writers seek to rid their garments of the blood of brethren who have dwindled in unbelief.

l: earth, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The earth was created by the word of God. In the day of visitation, it will be rolled together as a scroll and its elements will melt with fervent heat.

l: the ends of the earth, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The promise of answered prayer through belief in Christ is given to all, even unto the ends of the earth. Christ’s disciples are also commanded to preach the gospel to every creature, and Christ will confirm his words unto the ends of the earth.

l: the great and last day, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: At the great and last day, unbelievers will be brought to stand before the Lamb of God. They are urged to become spotless, pure, fair, and white through cleansing by the blood of the Lamb.

l: judgment, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: After all people are resurrected and stand before God’s bar, the judgment of the Holy One comes upon them. The filthy, righteous, happy, and unhappy remain as they are.

l: the fall of man, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The fall of man came through Adam. Because of the fall, Jesus Christ came, followed by the redemption of man.

l: redemption of the world, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The redemption of man came through Jesus Christ. Through it, people are brought back into the presence of the Lord, and the resurrection redeems all men from temporal death.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The death of Christ brings to pass the resurrection. By the power of God, all men will be awakened from an endless sleep and stand before God’s bar.

l: the death of Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The death of Christ brings to pass the resurrection and a redemption from an endless sleep. This sleep is identified with temporal death.

l: the second coming of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The text refers to the day when the Lord shall come, when the earth will be rolled together as a scroll and people will stand before the Lamb of God.

l: baptism, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Those who believe and are baptized shall be saved, while those who do not believe shall be damned. People are warned not to be baptized unworthily.

l: the sacrament of Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: People are warned not to partake of the sacrament of Christ unworthily. They are instructed to do all things in worthiness and in the name of Jesus Christ.

l: prayer, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: People are instructed to cry mightily unto the Father in the name of Jesus and to ask for whatever they need. The prayers of the saints concern the restoration of the brethren to the knowledge of Christ.

l: faith, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Those who believe in Christ without doubting may ask the Father in the name of Christ and receive what they ask. Faith is also connected with the prayers for the brethren and with the blessing of the house of Israel.

l: repentance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The text urges unbelievers to turn to the Lord, strip themselves of uncleanness, yield to no temptation, and serve the true and living God.

l: the signs of believers, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Signs follow those who believe in Christ’s name: they cast out devils, speak with new tongues, take up serpents, remain unharmed by deadly things, and heal the sick by laying on hands.

l: the gospel commission, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ commands his disciples to go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature. Believers who are baptized shall be saved, while those who do not believe shall be damned.

l: salvation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: People are told to work out their own salvation with fear and trembling before the Lord. Those who do all things in worthiness and endure to the end will in nowise be cast out.

l: covenant of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: God the Father made a covenant with the house of Israel. The text asks him to remember it and bless them forever through faith on the name of Jesus Christ.

l: the blood of the Lamb, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The blood of the Lamb cleanses those who turn to the Lord and seek to be spotless, pure, fair, and white at the great and last day.

l: the Book of Mormon record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The record was written according to the writers’ knowledge and contains imperfections because of their language and manner of speech. It was written to rid their garments of the blood of their brethren and to help restore them to the knowledge of Christ.

l: the plates, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The writers say that if their plates had been sufficiently large, they would have written in Hebrew.

l: reformed Egyptian, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The record was written in characters called among the writers the reformed Egyptian. Those characters were handed down and altered according to their manner of speech.

l: Hebrew, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 9
s: The writers say that Hebrew had also been altered by them. If they could have written in Hebrew, the record would have had no imperfection.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The Book of Ether is Moroni’s account of the Jaredites, drawn from the twenty and four plates found by the people of Limhi. It records the genealogy of Ether and describes Jared, the brother of Jared, and their people after the Lord confounded the language of the people at the great tower. The brother of Jared asked the Lord to preserve their language and the language of their friends, and the Lord directed them to gather their families, flocks, and seeds. The Lord promised to lead them from the valley which is northward into a choice land and to raise up a great nation from their descendants.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The Book of Ether is the record from which Moroni gives an account of the Jaredites. Its account begins at the tower and continues until the Jaredites were destroyed.

l: Jaredites, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The Jaredites came forth from the great tower with Jared, the brother of Jared, their families, and others. The Lord promised to lead them to a choice land and raise up a great nation from their descendants.

l: Moroni, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: Moroni gives an account of the ancient inhabitants who were destroyed in the north country. He takes his account from the twenty and four plates.

l: record of the Jaredites, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The record of the Jaredites was taken from the twenty-four plates found by the people of Limhi. It includes the genealogy of Ether and an account beginning at the tower.

l: twenty and four plates, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The twenty and four plates were found by the people of Limhi. Moroni takes his account of the Jaredites from them.

l: great tower, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: Jared, his brother, their families, and others came forth from the great tower when the Lord confounded the language of the people.

l: Ether, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: Ether wrote the record and was a descendant of Coriantor.

l: Jared, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: Jared asked his brother to cry unto the Lord so that their language would not be confounded. He later asked his brother to inquire where the Lord would lead them.

l: brother of Jared, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The brother of Jared was a large and mighty man who was highly favored of the Lord. He cried unto the Lord, and the Lord preserved the language of Jared, their friends, and their families, then directed him to gather them and go into the valley which is northward.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The Lord confounded the language of the people at the great tower and scattered them. He had compassion upon Jared, the brother of Jared, and their friends, and promised to lead them into a choice land and raise up a great nation.

l: language of the people, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The language of the people was confounded by the Lord at the great tower, causing the people to be scattered. The language of Jared, the brother of Jared, and their friends was not confounded.

l: valley of Nimrod, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The Lord directed the brother of Jared and the gathered people to go down into the valley which is northward, where He would meet them.

l: north country, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The ancient inhabitants described by Moroni were destroyed by the hand of the Lord upon the face of the north country.

l: confounding of the language, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The confounding of the language occurred at the great tower when the Lord swore that the people should be scattered over the face of the earth. Jared’s people and their friends were spared from this confounding.

l: scattering of the people, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The people were scattered upon all the face of the earth according to the word of the Lord after their language was confounded.

l: journey to the promised land, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The Lord told the brother of Jared to gather the people and go into the valley which is northward, promising to go before them into a choice land.

l: land of promise, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The Lord promised to lead Jared, the brother of Jared, their families, and their friends into a land which is choice above all the lands of the earth.

l: great nation, The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether / Chapter 1
s: The Lord promised to raise up a great nation from the seed of Jared, the brother of Jared, and those who would go with them. He said none would be greater than that nation upon all the face of the earth.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: Jared, the brother of Jared, their families, and their friends travel with animals, fowls, fish, bees, seeds, and other things into the wilderness under the direction of the Lord. They reach the great sea, call the place Moriancumer, and dwell there for four years before the Lord chastens the brother of Jared for failing to call upon him. The brother of Jared and his brethren build tight, light barges according to the Lord’s instructions, but the barges have no light and require holes for air. The Lord asks what should be done to provide light and explains that the people must be prepared to cross the great deep amid waves, winds, rains, and floods.

l: Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: Jared travels with his brother, their families, and their friends into the valley of Nimrod and then through the wilderness under the Lord’s direction. He is brought with his brethren to the great sea and dwells with them at Moriancumer for four years.

l: brother of Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The brother of Jared leads or joins the journey under the Lord’s direction and receives instructions from the Lord. After being chastened for not calling upon the Lord, he repents and builds barges with his brethren, then asks how they will breathe, steer, and have light in them.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The Lord directs Jared and his companions through the wilderness, brings them to the land of promise, chastens and forgives the brother of Jared, and instructs him to build barges. The Lord provides instructions for air holes and asks what should be done to give the barges light.

l: wilderness, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The wilderness is the region through which Jared, the brother of Jared, and their companions travel after the Lord commands them to go where no man had been. They build barges in the wilderness and cross many waters while being continually directed by the Lord.

l: land of promise, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The land of promise is described as choice above all other lands and preserved for a righteous people. Whoever possesses it must serve the true and only God or be swept off when the fulness of God’s wrath comes upon them.

l: God, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: God is identified as the true and only God whom the inhabitants of the land must serve. The text says that God’s wrath comes upon nations when they are ripened in iniquity.

l: Moriancumer, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: Moriancumer is the name Jared and his brethren give to the place where they pitch their tents beside the great sea. They dwell there in tents upon the seashore for four years.

l: great deep, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The great sea divides the lands, and Jared and his brethren reach it after traveling through the wilderness. They pitch their tents beside it at Moriancumer and are later prepared to cross its great depth in barges.

l: vessels or barges, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The barges are built small, light upon the water, and exceedingly tight, with peaked ends and a door that is tight when shut. They have no light, require holes in the top and bottom for air, and are intended to carry the people across the great water.

l: decrees of God, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The decrees of God concerning the land state that it is a land of promise and that any nation possessing it must serve God or be swept off when ripened in iniquity. The decrees are presented so the Gentiles may repent and avoid bringing down the fulness of God’s wrath.

l: the fullness of the Lord's wrath, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The fulness of the wrath of God comes upon the inhabitants of the land when they are ripened in iniquity. Nations that possess the land and do not serve God are threatened with being swept off.

l: building of the barges, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The building of the barges begins after the Lord commands the brother of Jared to work according to the manner of the barges previously built. The brother of Jared and his brethren build them according to the Lord’s instructions, making them small, light, and tight.

l: light, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: The barges have no light, and the brother of Jared asks the Lord whether the people must cross the great water in darkness. The Lord says they cannot use windows or fire and asks what should be done so they may have light in the vessels.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Ether, Chapter 2
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the God of the land who has been manifested by the things written in the record. The text says that the nation possessing the choice land can be free from bondage and captivity if it serves him.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: The brother of Jared asks the Lord to touch sixteen small stones so they will shine in the vessels and provide light while crossing the sea. The Lord touches the stones, reveals his finger, and then shows himself to the brother of Jared as Jesus Christ. Jesus Christ teaches that because of the brother of Jared’s faith, he is redeemed from the fall and brought into the Lord’s presence. The Lord shows him the inhabitants of the earth and commands him to write and seal what he has seen.

l: brother of Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: The brother of Jared makes sixteen small stones, asks the Lord to make them shine, and sees the finger of the Lord. Because of his faith and knowledge, he is brought into the Lord’s presence, sees Jesus Christ, and is shown the inhabitants of the earth. He is commanded to write and seal what he has seen and heard.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: Jesus Christ shows himself to the brother of Jared in the spirit and teaches that he is the Father and the Son. He says that he was prepared from the foundation of the world to redeem his people and that all mankind may have life through him.

l: small stones, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: The brother of Jared makes sixteen small stones from a rock. The Lord touches them one by one so they may shine in the vessels and provide light while the people cross the sea.

l: two stones, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: The Lord gives two stones to the brother of Jared. They are to be sealed with the things he writes and will magnify those writings to the eyes of men in the Lord’s due time.

l: finger of the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: The brother of Jared sees the finger of the Lord when the Lord touches the stones. It appears as the finger of a man, like flesh and blood, and causes the brother of Jared to fall with fear.

l: mankind, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: Jesus Christ says that all mankind may have life eternally by believing on his name. The Lord shows the brother of Jared all the inhabitants of the earth who had been and who would be.

l: fall, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: The text says that because of the fall, natures have become evil continually. Jesus Christ says that the brother of Jared is redeemed from the fall because of his faith.

l: incarnation, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: Jesus Christ says that he will take upon himself flesh and blood. He says that he will appear to his people in the flesh as he appears to the brother of Jared in the spirit.

l: redemption, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: Jesus Christ says that the brother of Jared is redeemed from the fall and therefore brought back into his presence.

l: faith, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: The brother of Jared’s faith enables him to see the finger of the Lord. Jesus Christ says that no man had come before him with such exceeding faith.

l: knowledge, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: The brother of Jared knows that the Lord speaks the truth and can show all things. Because of his knowledge, he cannot be kept from beholding within the veil.

l: flesh and blood, The Book of Ether, Chapter 3
s: The brother of Jared initially does not know that the Lord has flesh and blood. Jesus Christ teaches that he will take upon himself flesh and blood and appear to his people in the flesh.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The Lord commands the brother of Jared to write and seal the things he saw, including the interpretation, and says they will remain hidden until people repent and become clean. Jesus Christ promises to manifest greater revelations and the things seen by the brother of Jared to those who exercise faith and rend the veil of unbelief. The Gentiles and house of Israel are invited to come unto Christ, believe in his gospel, and receive knowledge of the things hidden from them. The Father’s work has commenced, and those who believe and are baptized in Christ’s name shall be saved.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: Jesus Christ commands that the things seen by the brother of Jared be made manifest after he has shown himself to his people. He promises to reveal greater things to those who exercise faith, condemns those who contend against or deny his word, and invites the Gentiles and house of Israel to come unto him, believe in his gospel, and be baptized in his name.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The Lord commands the brother of Jared to write the things he saw, seal them and their interpretation, and hide them again in the earth. He says they will not go forth unto the Gentiles until they repent of their iniquity and become clean before him.

l: brother of Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The brother of Jared sees things greater than any others made manifest, and the Lord commands him to write them. He exercises faith, and the things he saw are promised to those who later exercise faith as he did.

l: the Father, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The Father sent Jesus Christ and has laid up great things for the house of Israel from the foundation of the world. The Father remembers his covenant with their fathers, and his work has commenced upon all the face of the land.

l: Gentiles, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The Gentiles are told to come unto Jesus Christ, who will show them greater things and knowledge hidden because of unbelief. They are promised these things when they exercise faith and become sanctified.

l: the house of Israel, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The house of Israel is told that great things laid up by the Father will be made manifest to them. When they rend the veil of unbelief and call upon the Father with a broken heart and contrite spirit, they will know that the Father has remembered his covenant with their fathers.

l: plates, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The plates contain the things which the brother of Jared saw. The things on them are written and sealed, and the interpretation is also sealed according to the commandment of the Lord.

l: record, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The record is to be received as a sign that the work of the Father has commenced upon all the face of the land.

l: gospel of Christ, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: People throughout the earth are commanded to believe in the gospel of Christ. Those who believe and are baptized in Jesus Christ’s name shall be saved.

l: revelations, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The Lord promises to manifest all his revelations to those who exercise faith as the brother of Jared did. The revelations caused to be written by his servant John will be unfolded in the eyes of all the people when the time is at hand.

l: manifestations of the Spirit, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: Jesus Christ will visit those who believe his words with the manifestations of his Spirit, and they shall know and bear record.

l: Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The Spirit persuades people to do good, and through the Spirit a person can know that the things spoken are true. Whatever persuades people to do good is of Jesus Christ.

l: faith, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: Those who exercise faith in Jesus Christ and become sanctified in him will receive the things seen by the brother of Jared and all his revelations. Faith is also connected with believing, receiving manifestations of the Spirit, and salvation when joined with baptism.

l: unbelief, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: Unbelief causes knowledge and great things to remain hidden and leads people to remain in wickedness, hardness of heart, and blindness of mind. The veil of unbelief must be rent before the great and marvelous things can be made manifest.

l: repentance, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The Gentiles must repent of their iniquity and become clean before the Lord before the sealed things will go forth unto them. All the ends of the earth are commanded to repent and come unto Jesus Christ.

l: baptism, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: People are commanded to be baptized in Jesus Christ’s name. He that believes and is baptized shall be saved, while he that believes not shall be damned.

l: work of the Father, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The work of the Father has commenced upon all the face of the land when the record is received.

l: great and marvelous things, The Book of Ether, Chapter 4
s: The great and marvelous things hidden from the house of Israel from the foundation of the world will be made manifest when they rend the veil of unbelief and call upon the Father with a broken heart and contrite spirit.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: Moroni records the words he was commanded to write and says the sealed things must not be touched for translation except when God gives wisdom. He says the plates may be shown to those who assist in bringing forth the work, and that three witnesses will see them by the power of God. The testimony of the three witnesses, the work, and the records of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost will stand against the world at the last day, while those who repent and come to the Father in the name of Jesus will be received into the kingdom of God.

l: Moroni, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: Moroni writes the commanded words, recounts the sealed things, and says he has authority that will be known when he is seen and stands before God at the last day.

l: plates, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: The plates may be shown to those who assist in bringing forth the work, but they must not be touched for translation except when it is wisdom in God.

l: three witnesses, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: Three witnesses will be shown the plates by the power of God and will know with certainty that the things are true.

l: work, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: The work will show forth the power of God and his word, and it will stand with the testimony of three witnesses against the world at the last day.

l: God, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: God may grant wisdom concerning translation, show the plates to three witnesses by his power, and receive the repentant into his kingdom.

l: the Father, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: The Father is named as one of those who bear record of the work, and those who repent and come to him in the name of Jesus will be received into the kingdom of God.

l: the Son, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: The Son is named as one who bears record of the work.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: The Holy Ghost is named as one who bears record of the work.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: Those who repent and come unto the Father in the name of Jesus will be received into the kingdom of God.

l: testimony, The Book of Ether, Chapter 5
s: The testimony of three witnesses, together with the work and the records of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, will stand as a testimony against the world at the last day.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: Moroni records the voyage of Jared, the brother of Jared, and their people across the great waters to the promised land. The Lord makes stones shine in the vessels or barges, causes a furious wind to drive them toward the promised land, protects them on the sea, and brings them safely to shore after 344 days. After landing, the people till the earth, multiply, and become strong, while Jared and the brother of Jared gather them before their deaths. The people request a king, and Orihah is anointed and begins to reign.

l: Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: Jared travels with his people across the great waters and lands in the promised land. He has four sons, dies after gathering the people, and agrees that they may have a king.

l: brother of Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The brother of Jared places the prepared stones into the vessels or barges, and the stones give light. He travels with his people, teaches them to walk humbly before the Lord, gathers them before his death, and warns that having a king will lead into captivity.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The Lord causes the stones to shine, sends a furious wind toward the promised land, protects the vessels or barges from the waters, and brings them to the top of the waters when they cry unto him. He is praised by the people, who are taught from on high and taught to remember his great works.

l: Orihah, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: Orihah is the only one of Jared's sons who accepts being king, and he is anointed over the people. He begins to reign, and the people prosper and become exceedingly rich.

l: people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The people prepare food and animals, travel across the great waters, praise the Lord, and land in the promised land. They till the earth, multiply, wax strong, and request that one of the sons be anointed king over them.

l: promised land, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The promised land is the destination toward which the wind drives the people. After landing there, they till the earth, multiply, and become strong.

l: sea, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The sea has furious winds, mountain waves, deep waters, and terrible tempests that bury the vessels or barges. No monster of the sea or whale breaks or mars them, and the people travel upon the sea for 344 days.

l: small stones, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The brother of Jared carries the prepared stones into the vessels or barges, placing one in each end. The stones shine in darkness and give continual light above or under the water.

l: vessels or barges, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The vessels or barges carry the people, food, flocks, herds, beasts, animals, and fowls across the sea. They are tight like a dish and like the ark of Noah, so water cannot hurt the people inside.

l: light, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The stones provide light in the vessels or barges so that the people do not cross the great waters in darkness. They have light continually, whether above or under the water.

l: wind, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The Lord causes a furious wind to blow toward the promised land. The wind never ceases while the people are upon the waters and drives them forward.

l: bringing them across the great deep, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The people travel across the great waters in their vessels or barges, enduring deep waters, mountain waves, and terrible tempests. They are driven before the wind for 344 days and praise the Lord throughout the voyage.

l: landing in the promised land, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The people land upon the shore of the promised land after 344 days upon the water. They bow down, humble themselves before the Lord, and shed tears of joy because of his tender mercies.

l: anointing a king, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The people request that one of the sons of Jared or the brother of Jared be anointed king. After several sons refuse, Orihah is anointed king over the people.

l: kingship, The Book of Ether, Chapter 6
s: The brother of Jared says that kingship will lead into captivity, while Jared allows the people to choose a king. The chosen sons refuse except Orihah, who begins to reign and leads the people into prosperity.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Orihah is succeeded by Kib, who is taken captive after his son Corihor rebels, captures the king in Moron, and draws away many people. Shule strengthens himself, defeats Corihor, restores the kingdom to Kib, and later reigns in righteousness, while Noah rebels against Shule, captures him, and is slain by Shule’s sons. The land is divided between the kingdom of Shule and the kingdom of Cohor, but Shule defeats Cohor and receives the kingdom through Nimrod. Prophets warn that the people’s wickedness and idolatry will bring destruction, and Shule’s judgments cause the people to repent, after which they prosper and have no more wars during his days.

l: Kib, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Kib reigns after Orihah and begets Corihor. Corihor takes Kib captive, and Kib remains in captivity until old age, when he begets Shule; after Shule defeats Corihor, Kib’s kingdom is restored to him and he bestows it upon Shule.

l: Corihor, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Corihor rebels against his father Kib, dwells in the land of Nehor, draws away many people, and captures the king in Moron. Shule defeats him and restores the kingdom to Kib; Corihor later repents of his evils and receives power in Shule’s kingdom.

l: Shule, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Shule becomes mighty in strength and judgment, makes steel swords at the hill Ephraim, defeats Corihor, and restores the kingdom to Kib. He reigns in righteousness, defeats Noah’s forces, is rescued after being taken captive, gives Corihor power, executes judgment against those who revile the prophets, and rules during a time of prosperity and no wars.

l: Noah, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Noah, a son of Corihor, rebels against Shule and his father, drawing away Cohor, his brethren, and many people. He battles Shule, takes him captive into Moron, and is slain by Shule’s sons while preparing to put Shule to death.

l: the prophets, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Prophets come among the people during Shule’s reign, warning that wickedness and idolatry are bringing a curse upon the land and that the people will be destroyed unless they repent. The people revile and mock them, but Shule gives the prophets power to go wherever they will.

l: people, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: The people become exceedingly numerous and are drawn away by Corihor and Noah during their rebellions. They revile and mock the prophets, then repent of their iniquities and idolatries and begin to prosper again.

l: kingdom of Shule, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: The kingdom of Shule is established when Shule receives the kingdom from Kib. It remains under Shule’s rule after the land is divided, and Nimrod gives the kingdom of Cohor to Shule.

l: judgment, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Orihah executes judgment in righteousness throughout his days, and Shule is mighty in judgment. Shule executes judgment against those who revile the prophets and continues to execute judgment in righteousness throughout his reign.

l: captivity, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Kib dwells in captivity under Corihor until he becomes exceedingly old. Noah takes Shule captive and carries him into Moron, but Shule’s sons break open the prison and bring him out.

l: rebellion, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Corihor rebels against his father Kib and draws away many people. Noah later rebels against Shule and Corihor, drawing away Cohor, his brethren, and many of the people.

l: battle, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Shule gives battle to Corihor and obtains the kingdom, then battles Noah and his people. Shule defeats Cohor’s people and slays Cohor.

l: repentance, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: Corihor repents of the many evils he has done, and Shule gives him power in the kingdom. The people later repent of their iniquities and idolatries, after which the Lord spares them and they prosper.

l: wickedness, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: The prophets warn that the wickedness of the people is bringing a curse upon the land and will lead to destruction if they do not repent.

l: idolatry, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: The prophets warn that the people’s idolatry is bringing a curse upon the land. When the people repent of their idolatries, the Lord spares them and they prosper again.

l: wars, The Book of Ether, Chapter 7
s: The people engage in wars during the conflicts involving Corihor, Noah, and Cohor. There are no more wars in the days of Shule.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Jared rebelled against his father, Omer, gained half the kingdom through flattering many people, and took Omer into captivity. Esrom and Coriantumr defeated Jared's army, but Jared was spared and became sorrowful over losing the kingdom. Jared's daughter devised a plan, danced before Akish, and persuaded Jared to promise her in marriage if Akish brought Omer's head. Akish formed a secret combination through oaths, and Moroni warned that such combinations bring murder, destruction, and the loss of freedom, while urging the Gentiles to repent.

l: Omer, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Omer reigned after his father and was Jared's father. Jared took him into captivity, where Omer spent half of his reign and begat Esrom and Coriantumr.

l: Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Jared rebelled against Omer, gained half the kingdom by flattering people, and took Omer captive. After Esrom and Coriantumr defeated his army, Jared surrendered the kingdom and became sorrowful over its loss.

l: Akish, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Akish was the son of Kimnor and a friend of Omer. Jared's daughter pleased him by dancing, and Akish formed a secret combination after Jared promised her to him if he brought Omer's head.

l: Moroni, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Moroni wrote that he would not describe the oaths and combinations because they were known among all people and among the Lamanites. He warned that these combinations cause destruction and urged the Gentiles to repent.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: God is presented as opposing secret combinations and the shedding of blood. The Lord forbids such acts, warns nations that uphold them of destruction, and commands the Gentiles to awake and repent.

l: Satan, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Satan is described as the father of all lies and the builder of secret combinations. He seeks to gain power over people's hearts and has caused murder and opposition to the prophets.

l: daughter of Jared, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Jared's daughter was exceedingly expert and fair. She devised a plan to redeem the kingdom to Jared, taught him about ancient secret plans, and proposed dancing before Akish to secure a marriage arrangement.

l: Gentiles, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: The Gentiles are warned to repent and not allow murderous combinations to gain power over them. They are told to awake to their awful situation when such combinations appear among them.

l: kingdom, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Jared gained half of the kingdom through flattering people and later lost the kingdom after Esrom and Coriantumr defeated his army. Jared's daughter sought to redeem the kingdom to him.

l: captivity of Omer, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Omer was carried into captivity by Jared and served in captivity for half of his reign. During that time, he begat Esrom and Coriantumr.

l: Jared's rebellion, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Jared rebelled against Omer, moved to the land of Heth, and used cunning words to gain half the kingdom. He then gave battle to Omer and made him serve in captivity.

l: daughter of Jared's dance, The Book of Ether, Chapter 8
s: Jared's daughter danced before Akish and pleased him so that he desired her as a wife. Jared offered her to Akish if Akish would bring Omer's head.
